chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Salih al-Qadhi reported to us, saying: Masrooq ibn al-Marzban reported to us, saying: Hafs reported to us, from Asim, from Abu Uthman, from Abu Hurayra who said:

The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, said: "Indeed, the most helpless of people is one who is unable to make supplication, and indeed the most miserly of people is one who is miserly with the greeting of peace."

key_terms.الدعاء: Du'a (supplication), the act of calling upon God in prayer
key_terms.السلام: Salam (peace greeting), the Islamic greeting of peace

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about supplication and greeting others with salam?
ai.summary: The Prophet (SAWW) identifies two of the worst human failings: being too heedless to supplicate to God, and being too stingy to greet others with salam. This hadith, narrated through Abu Hurayra in a Sunni-Shia shared chain, was delivered as part of the Prophet's general moral counsel to his community. The original audience understood supplication (du'a) as a fundamental act of worship showing dependence on God, and salam as the basic social bond between believers, making neglect of either a mark of spiritual and social deficiency.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 2. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji’abi reported to me from Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Swaleh al-Qadhi, who reported from Masrooq ibn al-Marzban, who reported from Hafs, from Asim, from Abu Uthman, from Abu Huraira, who said:

The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said: "The most helpless person is the one who renders himself unable to supplicate (to Allah), and the most niggardly is the one who is miserly with greeting in salaam."
